title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Null Result on a Deterministic Synthetic Task Pool
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measures the marginal operational effect of inserting a verifier+repair layer (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) versus accepting an LLM‑only suggestion for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and deterministic validator, we sampled K=200 paired tasks and produced one shared initial candidate per task with gpt-5-mini. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in regression‑causing change rate (guarded − baseline). Observed outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies, guarded = 200/200 (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; bootstrap [10,000 resamples, seed=1729] 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]). The repair loop never invoked (repair_applied = 0). We release complete execution and analysis artifacts (prompts, provider traces, validator traces, manifests, and hashes) to enable exact replay and discuss why the null arose and how future confirmatory designs should avoid ceiling effects.

sections.introduction: Automating the translation from operator intent to concrete device configuration promises operational efficiency for NetOps, but unsafe or regression‑inducing proposals present real risk when applied at scale. One widely proposed mitigation is to place a deterministic verifier (an emulator or formal checker) between generation and apply, and to optionally invoke an automated repair step when the verifier rejects a candidate: a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline. Prior proposals and benchmarks argue such verifier‑guided loops improve reliability, but rigorous, preregistered measurements of the marginal operational benefit are scarce because outcomes depend on the task distribution, generator fidelity, and validator realism. We therefore preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment intended to isolate the marginal value of the verifier+repair layer while holding the generator output fixed. The run was executed autonomously under Master Prompt v1 (immutable archived reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and followed the frozen preregistration (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop, preregistration SHA‑256: a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622). This paper reports the preregistered design, complete artifact trace, confirmatory inference, and a grounded interpretation of the null outcome.
sections.related_work: Two strands of literature frame our contribution. First, generator‑centric work explores LLMs that convert intent→configuration, and many recent studies document promising task‑level synthesis quality in controlled settings (example leads: Cornetto; translation‑plus‑solver position papers). Second, verifier‑centric work uses formal, symbolic, or emulated checks to guarantee safety before a change is applied; several systems and benchmarks emphasize closed‑loop generate→validate→repair evaluation. Recent agentic‑NetOps surveys and tool‑augmented self‑correction research motivate verifier integration and automated repair (see the manuscript evidence bundle for the closest verified sources cited in our preregistration). Our experiment sits between these axes: it is a preregistered, paired evaluation that explicitly measures the marginal effect of adding verifier/repair when the generator’s proposal is fixed and reproducibly logged.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The full preregistration (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) froze the research question, primary/secondary estimands, deterministic sampling, and the exact analysis plan prior to execution. Primary hypothesis H1: the G→V→R pipeline yields a lower regression‑causing change rate than LLM‑only (paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference (guarded minus baseline) in the proportion of tasks that fail post‑apply regression tests.
Design and determinism: To isolate verifier/repair marginal effects we used a paired, shared_initial_generation design. For each sampled intent a single candidate configuration was generated (shared_initial_generation) by the requested model (gpt-5-mini, see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). That candidate was scored in two ways: (a) baseline—simulating operator accept of the LLM suggestion; (b) guarded—validator evaluates candidate, and if invalid the preregistered guarded policy allowed one repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were required by the preregistration; only tasks the validator could cover were eligible. Sampling was deterministic: compute SHA‑256(intent_string), sort ascending, and select the first K=200 tasks. The preregistration specified planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs) and maximum_model_calls = 400. The run adhered to these constraints (see execution manifest). All per‑call prompt/response artifacts, provider headers, and validator traces were archived and hashed to support exact replay.
Task pool and validator coverage: The sampled pool was constructed from a public synthetic intent corpus restricted to intents whose required features lay inside the validator coverage matrix (allowed_fields in transformation_manifest.json included {"admin","mtu","vlan"}). This preregistered filter ensured that the deterministic validator could deterministically parse, evaluate, and return structured verdicts (validator outputs include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_codes). Tasks retained by the filter are therefore within the validator’s semantically analyzable fragment; tasks outside coverage were excluded automatically and logged (exclusion manifest recorded in execution/).
sections.results:
Execution completeness and artifact accounting: The autonomous run completed exactly as preregistered. Start/completion timestamps and the full execution manifest are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256: 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). Completed episodes = 400 (200 paired tasks), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task). Provider call traces are available under execution/provider_calls/*.json and response files under execution/responses/*.txt; per‑task scoring/validator traces are in execution/scoring/*.json.
Confirmatory outcome: For every sampled task the generated candidate passed the deterministic validator in both arms. Counts: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test returns p = 1.00. The preregistered bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) percentile 95% CI for the paired difference is [0.00, 0.00]. The repair pathway was never invoked (aggregate repair_applied = 0); validator traces consistently show validator.valid = true and normalized_configuration equal to the shared initial candidate (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json and similar files for tasks 000001–000200).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and ceiling effect: The preregistered objective was to measure whether verifier+repair reduces regression‑causing changes compared to accepting the LLM suggestion. The observed degenerate null arises because the shared initial generation produced validator‑compliant candidates for every sampled intent; the verifier never needed to block or repair, hence no discordant pairs were possible. This outcome is a classical ceiling effect that invalidates the preregistered power assumption (the preregistration assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.20 and targeted an absolute reduction of 0.08). We emphasize the empirical lesson: a confirmatory demonstration of verifier/repair value requires either (i) a task distribution with non‑negligible baseline error probability under the chosen generator, (ii) weaker / perturbed generator outputs, or (iii) designs that permit generator adaptation to verifier feedback (interactive generator–verifier loops). Any of those changes alter the estimand and must be preregistered.
Operational implications: The null does not imply that verifiers are unnecessary in practice. In an operational deployment the generator may be less deterministic or may operate on production intents outside a narrow validator fragment. Here, the deterministic generator + curated validator coverage produced a regime where LLM proposals were within the validator’s safety envelope. For practitioners this suggests two operationally useful takeaways: (1) verify validator coverage relative to intended change classes before investing in a closed‑loop repair pipeline; (2) measure baseline generator failure rates on production logs or deliberately perturbed prompts to assess whether verifier investment is expected to yield measurable risk reductions.
Methodological lessons for confirmatory NetOps evaluation: Our preregistered shared_initial_generation design isolates verifier marginal effects but reduces ecological realism: operational agentic workflows more typically involve iterative generator–verifier interactions (generator sees validator feedback and regenerates). Such interactive designs may better capture real deployment architectures but require different estimands and careful preregistration of interaction protocols. Additionally, deterministic synthetic task pools—useful for reproducibility—must be balanced to avoid ceiling or floor effects; we recommend including stratified failure‑rich subsets or adversarial perturbations in future confirmatory plans.
Reproducibility and auditability: We release the complete artifact set required for exact replay: master prompt provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba), preregistration JSON (SHA‑256: a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256: 3dfbe1b6...), per‑task responses (execution/responses/*.txt), provider traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), and validator scoring traces (execution/scoring/*.json). Deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms accounting consistency across artifacts. The archived artifacts permit auditors to verify that (a) generation calls were shared per task, (b) no post‑hoc design changes occurred, and (c) the validator verdicts and scoring decisions are recoverable and deterministic.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, autonomous paired comparison of G→V→R versus LLM‑only suggestions on a deterministic synthetic NetOps task pool. The confirmatory result is a degenerate null driven by a ceiling effect: the shared generator output was validator‑compliant for every sampled task (200/200 successes in both arms), so the verifier/repair layer never engaged. This outcome is artifact‑grounded and reproducible: all prompts, responses, provider traces, validator traces, manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed to permit exact replay. The principal methodological conclusion is practical: to demonstrate verifier/repair utility in a confirmatory test one must avoid ceiling conditions by sampling failure‑rich tasks, weakening or perturbing the generator, or adopting an interactive generator–verifier protocol and preregistering the corresponding estimand. We provide the full artifact bundle to support future preregistered designs that address these constraints.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without further experiments.
Synthetic deterministic task pool and preregistered validator filter — external validity to production change intents is limited.
Primary outcome depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; construct validity hinges on validator realism and coverage.
Ceiling effect: baseline success = 100% eliminated the ability to demonstrate verifier/repair benefit under this design and sample.
Residual contamination (undetectable pretraining overlap) cannot be fully excluded despite hashing and logging; contamination_summary.csv recorded no flagged items for this run.
